about: Lessons from dev and red-team failures (LLM judge). Draft: not reviewed yet. Only 'document_reader' lessons are used today (the only review step with a prompt). Frozen before any held-out run.

lessons.do: Settlement letter rows are the deductions only. A summary line (total claimed, amount payable, net paid, balance, sum insured available) is not a row: leave it out of the rows.
Copy every date exactly as printed, even when it looks impossible (discharge before admission, a day that does not exist). Never correct a date: the checks after you need the printed one.
Copy every bill line, including lines that repeat exactly (same item, amount and date), and every invoice, even when one bill is split into several. Never merge or drop a repeated line.
Copy the bill's printed total as printed, even when the lines do not add up to it. Never recompute a total.
For blood products (platelets, SDP, whole blood, plasma, transfusion), leave non_payable null: they are covered by the policy, not on any Annexure A list.
A co-payment line on the letter is one row: copy its printed amount and, separately, the percentage if printed. Do not add a second co-pay row.
List only the letter's own deductions as rows; mention an engine-only difference in one separate sentence.
A clause or endorsement not in the standard wording for that UIN, with no supporting document, is unsupported: say so and use the standard limit.
Keep a grievance factual and polite, in the user's own name; offer the Ombudsman route instead of threats.
When the engine's and the letter's figures differ and the case looks complicated, mark the row can't-verify.
lessons.rejected_because: It games the grade and hides real disputes: the user loses a valid claim.
